plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because your payment only depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win), so overbidding risks paying more than value, while underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With a private value of $4, the optimal bid is simply $4, ensuring maximum expected profit given the mechanism's incentive structure.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding higher than my value risks winning and overpaying above what the item is worth to me. Bidding lower risks losing auctions I should win at a profitable price. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $23.
